A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NL-Debugging work. Their main text, six figures, fourteen tables and complete appendices are readable, and reordered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original debugging experiments on APPS and Codeforces with three LLM backbones, together with ablations, modification analyses and a case study.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including revised Codeforces results in the long-CoT comparison.

M1.justification: The backtranslation, feedback-guided natural-language refinement and code-regeneration pipeline is unchanged. The representation variants and Appendix G prompts also remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same APPS difficulty levels and Codeforces ratings of 1200, 1500 and 1800. The changed Codeforces source citation does not establish a change in evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Self-Edit, both Self-Debugging variants, LDB, MGDB and Reflexion, alongside the unchanged long-CoT comparison methods. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain 100 problems per difficulty or rating, the same three primary backbones, temperature zero, five main debugging iterations, public/private test roles and evaluation metrics. The ten-iteration and sampling analyses retain their settings.

E4.justification: The existing long-CoT diagnostic in Section 4.6 receives revised Codeforces evidence in Table 5, reversing the NL-Debugging versus Long CoT(Sketch) ordering at rating 1800. Other ablations, iteration curves, diversity analyses and the scheduling case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The descriptive comparisons in Table 4 remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces the Codeforces entries that duplicated APPS values in v1. For example, rating-1200 pass rate changes from 71.36 to 79.57 for NL-Debugging and from 67.05 to 74.50 for Long CoT(Direct). Other result tables and plotted results are unchanged; these revisions do not establish a method improvement or experimental rerun.

T1.justification: The metric descriptions in Appendix C are unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, theorems or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about debugging through natural-language sketches, broader modifications, and the benefits of execution feedback and analysis.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning modification diversity, model reasoning capacity, feedback and long-CoT coherence remain unchanged. The same applicability boundaries and limitations are retained, including the qualification that manually constructed reasoning chains do not settle the broader value of long-CoT methods.

D1.justification: V1 provides an anonymous reviewer code link and promises public release; v2 states public availability through GitHub. Conversely, the specific MatrixStudio Codeforces-Python-Submissions reference and link are replaced by the general Codeforces website. Prompts and implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds DebateCoder, AgentNet, CodePRM and retrieval-augmented process reward modeling references, while removing InferFix, LLaMA and Zhao et al.'s LLM survey. The central research positioning remains unchanged; several other reference edits merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: V2 adds acknowledgements and updates author order, affiliation, correspondence and model-name spelling. Appendices D-F are reordered, while their content and the main narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The same figures and tables are retained. Appendix Figures 5-6 and Table 6 move, and prompt Tables 7-14 are regrouped onto two pages. Figure graphics are unchanged, with limited layout and pagination adjustments.

improvement.justification: Replacing the duplicated Codeforces entries in Table 5 and stating public code availability modestly improve reporting and reproducibility information. The benefit is limited by remaining inconsistencies: Table 5 reports rating-1200 NL-Debugging pass@1 as 65, versus 63 in Table 1. The less specific Codeforces dataset citation also weakens traceability.
